summary: This roadmap develops geometric Enriques surfaces over arbitrary fields and flat proper algebraic-space families, their canonical degree-two covers, characteristic-two types and numerical lattices. It combines Picard descent, dyadic twisting, finite-field genus-one fibrations and lattice configuration arguments to plan integral and F₂ nonexistence. The endpoints retain explicit completeness, omitted-configuration and source-acquisition gates rather than claiming that these gaps are proved.

nodes.title: Enriques surface

hypotheses: For III* exclusions, Y/F₂ is nonexceptional with constant full Picard and both classification gates. For restricted-configurations-impossible, k is algebraically closed of arbitrary characteristic and Y is classical, with the two global configuration restrictions stated there.
All additional alternatives, scheme multiplicities, local-base conditions and field restrictions stated in this target are retained.
proofSteps: In characteristic two use ESB exceptional-fibration classification to exclude exceptional surfaces from these global restrictions; in other characteristics use the general partner theorem directly. Thus every chosen half-fibre has a partner. This preserves the original arbitrary-characteristic scope.

For an I₁* fibration the partner completion either contradicts half-fibre intersection one or yields a IV* canonical-type curve. Then exclude a multiple I₂* by an I₀* completion. Finally all I₂* fibres are simple and both III fibres multiple; the horizontal components of two partner III fibres together with those of the original pair produce an I₄ canonical-type curve, outside the allowed global restrictions.
acceptance: Keep the stated field, multiplicity and Picard hypotheses; give the proof on the actual geometric objects.
